question:
What general practices should developers follow when writing code so that attackers cannot exploit it?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Developers should follow secure coding practices spanning input validation, privilege management, error handling, dependency management, and design principles to reduce vulnerabilities that attackers could exploit throughout the software development lifecycle.

# Guidelines

- Validate all input to prevent malformed or malicious data from entering the system. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Top 10 Software Security Practices.md)
- Heed compiler warnings and keep designs simple, applying default deny policies. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Best Practices and Design Principles.md)
- Adhere to the principle of least privilege and sanitize data sent to other software. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Best Practices for Software Development.md)
- Practice defense in depth and use effective quality assurance techniques. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Software Security Best Practices.md)
- Keep privileged modules as small as possible, validate all program assumptions, and check every function's error status. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Secure Module Design and Error Handling Principles.md)
- Structure code so sections requiring extra privileges are isolated modules. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Secure Software Design and Implementation Practices/Software Construction Security and Privilege Management.md)
- Prevent code-level security breaches such as buffer overflows or array index bounds violations. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Software Coding and Construction Testing Practices.md)
- Use assertions and defensive programming, checking values of all [SWEBOK excerpt dda5a39412b3af36208d]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Contract Design and Error Handling Strategies/Design by Contract and Defensive Programming.md)
- Design exception-handling policies carefully, including all information that led to the exception and avoiding empty catch blocks. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Contract Design and Error Handling Strategies/Error Handling, Exception Handling, and Fault Tolerance.md)
- Use sound coding practices and refer to vulnerability databases such as CVE, CWE, and CAPEC during security implementation. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Security Development and Testing Practices/Security Testing and Vulnerability Detection/Vulnerability Detection and Analysis Tools/Vulnerability Management and Security Tools.md)
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies and prevent introduction of untrusted external dependencies to reduce supply chain risk. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Methods and Languages/Dependency Management and Construction Practices/Managing Software Dependencies and Supply Chain Risks.md)
- [SWEBOK excerpt 9536bea715ff8d35654a], using automated static code analysis for security weaknesses. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Construction Quality Techniques and Practices.md)
- Choose programming languages carefully, as the choice [SWEBOK excerpt bee614598732f0777be8]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Methods and Languages/Programming Language Notation and Security Implications/Programming Language Notations and Security Considerations.md)
- Build security into software engineering from the start rather than as an afterthought, following a secure development lifecycle. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Security Engineering and Professional Practice/Secure Software Development Standards and Practices/Security Integration and Evaluation Standards/Security Engineering and Secure Development Life Cycle.md)
